_meta.indication: Prophylaxis of cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection and disease in adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial; subjects randomized 2:1 to PREVYMIS 480 mg once daily (adjusted to 240 mg with cyclosporine) or placebo, started after HSCT and continued through Week 14 post-transplant.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of an allogeneic hematopoietic stem cell transplant (HSCT).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: The incidence of clinically significant CMV infection through Week 24 post-transplant (prophylaxis failure), defined as CMV end-organ disease or initiation of anti-CMV pre-emptive therapy based on documented CMV viremia.
pivotal_trials.n: Efficacy population of 495 subjects: 325 received PREVYMIS and 170 received placebo.
pivotal_trials.result: Prophylaxis failure through Week 24 occurred in 38% of letermovir subjects vs 61% of placebo; clinically significant CMV infection by Week 24 in 18% vs 42%. Stratum-adjusted treatment difference -23.5 (95% CI -32.5, -14.6); p<0.0001.

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥10% and ≥2% greater than placebo) were nausea (27% vs 23%), diarrhea (26% vs 24%), vomiting (19% vs 14%), peripheral edema (14% vs 9%), cough (14% vs 10%), headache (14% vs 9%), fatigue (13% vs 11%), and abdominal pain (12% vs 9%). Cardiac adverse event rate was higher with PREVYMIS (13%) vs placebo (6%).
target_moa: Letermovir is an inhibitor of the CMV DNA terminase complex (encoded by UL56/UL89), which is necessary for generation of unit-length viral DNA genomes; this is a novel mechanism of action distinct from DNA polymerase inhibitors.
modality: Small molecule (antiviral agent; new molecular entity).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application was not referred because outside expertise was not necessary and there were no controversial issues.

summary.text: Letermovir (PREVYMIS), a new molecular entity CMV terminase inhibitor, was granted Fast Track (2011), Orphan Drug (2011), and Breakthrough Therapy (2017) designations, and was reviewed under Priority review; it received traditional (non-accelerated) first-cycle approval on the strength of Phase 3 trial P001.

On May 25, 2011, FDA granted Fast Track designation to letemovir for the prevention of human CMV disease in transplant recipients.
On December 12, 2011, FDA approved the request for Orphan drug designation for letemovir for the prevention of human CMV viremia and disease in at risk populations.

On February 27, 2017, Breakthrough therapy designation was granted for IV and oral letemovir for the prevention of CMV infection and/or disease in adult CMV-seropositive recipients [R+] of allogeneic HSCT.

The clinical efficacy and safety of letemovir is primarily supported by one phase 3 trial (P001) evaluating letemovir (tablets and intravenous solution) compared to placebo and one phase 2b dose-ranging trial (P020) that also included a placebo comparison.
